newsitem.title: UK: Lebanon PM sees 1997 growth rising above six pct.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon PM sees 1997 growth rising above six pct.

text.p: Lebanon's Prime Minister, Rafik Al-Hariri, said on Thursday his country's economic growth in 1997 should exceed six percent, above 1996's rate of five percent.

"The growth in the economy last year was over five percent," he told Reuters Financial Television. "We are expecting this year more than six percent and (for) the last three years...the average was over seven percent."
Hariri said his government was trying to improve an economy damaged by war.

"We are upgrading the economic life as well as the social life. We have increased salaries several times, we have increased the budget for healthcare, for public transportation, for schooling, for university," he said.
Asked about rising deficit and public debt levels, he said: "I am concerned, not worried. We have to increase our revenue."
Hariri said revenue in 1992 was about 10 percent of spending needs.

"The deficit now is still high, I agree with that. But where is the money going? Mostly for salaries and to service the debt, very little for construction and investment. Most of the investment projects are coming from outside."
